body.statement: The coordinate projection of a semialgebraic subset of a finite-dimensional real space is semialgebraic.  Every semialgebraic subset of \(\mathbb R\) has finitely many connected components, each an interval or a point.

source.verbatim_statement: Then Π(S) is a semi-algebraic subset of Rⁿ. Every semi-algebraic set has a finite number of connected components, which are semi-algebraic.

attestation.note: Verified 2026-09-13 against Springer’s official chapter PDF for Semi-algebraic Sets, DOI chapter 10.1007/978-3-662-03718-8_3: Theorem 2.2.1 (printed p. 27), Theorem 2.4.5 (printed p. 35); Proposition 2.5.13 additionally identifies semialgebraic connectedness with semialgebraic path connectedness.
